text.p: PRAVDA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said the government would, by the end of this year, work out a document defining its strategy for restructuring banks.
- Kozlik said the 1997 draft budget will bring strong development impulses, mainly in the field of infrastructure and exports, which is expected to result in reduction of the unemployment.
- Kozlik rejected information that he planned to resign.
- The northern Slovak region of the High Tatras will make a bid for winter Olympic games in 2006.

NARODNA OBRODA - State-owned gas distributor SPP said it wanted to acquire stakes of about 10 percent in two Czech gas distributors, Severomoravska Plynarenska a.s. (SP) and Vychodoceska Plynarenska a.s. by the end of the year. The SPP said it would later try to acquire a major part of the 46- percent stake in SP, currently held by the Czech National Property Fund.
- The average wage in industrial sector increased by 10.6 percent year-on-year in September, to 8,091 crowns, but was 2.7 percent lower than in August.

- Roman Hofbauer, a deputy of the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) and chairman of the parliamentary privatisation committee, said he expected a "third wave" of privatisation, which should re-distribute the property privatised in the second wave.
- The legislation council of the government is discussing the revised version of the controversial draft law on protection of republic, proposed by deputies of the ruling coalition.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Engineering company and major arms producer ZVS Dubnica said it would need a contract from the army worth at least 300 million crowns next year to help solve its financial problems.
- About 70 percent of citizens who hold privatisation bonds will not sell their bonds under the minimum guaranteed price of 7,500 crowns, an opinion poll showed.
- Slovakia and Austria on Wednesday inaugurated a joint chamber of commerce which should intensify the mutual trade between the two countries.
